rules.dispatch: post/pre BITVECTOR_SLT via RewriteSlt (after EvalSlt, SltSelf); ProofRewriteRule MACRO_BV_MULT_SLT_MULT elaborated by MacroRewriteElaborator::ensureProofForMultSltMult
rules.guard_comparison: extract_ext_tuple returns (zext-arg, sext-arg) for the mixed concat/sext case, but applies() then lets the ADD be either ml[0] or ml[1] and lets a match either mr[0] or mr[1], ignoring which operand is zero- vs sign-extended; RARE -2 only covers zext(x+t)*sext(a) vs zext(x)*sext(a). Also concat(0, y, z, ...) with >2 children is treated as zext(y) (dropping z, and the size guard only checks |y|), and the elaborator turns it into an ill-typed (zero_extend |0| y). The final elaboration step is a MACRO_THEORY_REWRITE_RCONS_SIMPLE trust that stays unproved on all mismatched shapes. sext/sext and correctly-ordered mixed forms reconstruct cleanly. Upstream PR #13042 (not in pinned rev 40a4bb7e43) requires 2-child concat, requires the ADD in the zext position (ml[0]) and a in the sext position on the right (mr[1]) in the mixed case: by inspection this closes all three gap classes found here, leaving only the shapes RARE -1/-2 cover. Binary dc8ad24031 additionally predates the (>= n tn) (>= m an) guards on bv-mult-slt-mult-1/2 (aafcc486e2), irrelevant to these witnesses since C++ checks sizes.
rules.guard_gap: Mixed zext/sext case where the zero-extended operand is a (not x+t) on either side, or concat with >2 children. Three classes: (1) L zext(a)*sext(x+t), R zext(a)*sext(x) [#13039]; (2) a zero-extended on one side and sign-extended on the other (L zext(x+t)*sext(a), R zext(a)*sext(x); or L zext(a)*sext(x+t), R zext(x)*sext(a)); (3) n-ary concat(0, x+t, z) * sext(a) vs concat(0, x, z2) * sext(a).
